author: Gmelin, 1788
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수백 마리

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 알 낳는 시기는 5~6월이다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 지나가는 나그네새이며, 드물게 번식하기도 한다. 숲, 농경지, 트인 땅에서 관찰된다. 큰 나무의 가지 위에 마른 나뭇가지로 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고, 5~6월에 푸른빛이 도는 흰 알 2~4개를 낳는다. 아시아 동부 온대, 아무르 남부, 우수리, 일본, 만주, 중국에 분포하며 동남아시아에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: brown from forehead to uppertail coverts
white in the hindcrown and hindneck feathers
bill yellow at the base with a black tip
broad brown-and-white bars on lower breast, belly and flanks

art.subject: Grey-faced Buzzard (Butastur indicus), adult, as seen on spring passage in Korea in April–May: crown and upperparts brown, with white feather bases showing on the hindcrown and nape; face and ear-coverts grey; throat white with a single dark stripe down the centre; upper breast plain rusty-brown; lower breast, belly and flanks broadly barred brown and white; undertail coverts white; tail grey-brown with three or four narrow dark bands. Small hooked bill black at the tip, yellow at the base, with a yellow cere; yellow eye; dull yellow legs.
art.pose: perched on a branch at a forest edge overlooking farmland
art.scene: Korean spring migration: woodland edge beside open farmland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched: brown upperparts with white on the nape, grey face, white throat with a dark central stripe, rusty-brown upper breast, barred belly, yellow-based black-tipped bill, yellow eye, dull yellow legs
adult, front view perched: white throat with one dark central stripe, plain rusty-brown upper breast, broad brown-and-white bars on the lower breast, belly and flanks, grey face
adult in flight seen from below: long, fairly narrow wings with pale, finely barred underwing, rusty-brown breast, barred belly, tail with narrow dark bands, head, body and tail in a straight line
art.build: Medium-sized, slim raptor, a little smaller than a crow, built like a long-winged buzzard with a slimmer body and longer tail. Head rounded, neck short. Bill small and hooked, much shorter than the head. Legs medium length, dull yellow, the tarsi unfeathered. At rest the long wingtips reach well down the tail, short of the tip. In flight long, fairly narrow wings and a medium-long, square-ended tail; often glides on flat wings and migrates in flocks.
avoid: Do not paint a chunky, broad-winged Common Buzzard with a pale breast band; this species is slimmer and longer-winged.
Do not omit the grey face or the dark central stripe on the white throat.
Do not paint feathered legs or an unbanded tail.
Do not give it a large, deep eagle bill.
